subject: Commitment stretch: containment protocol and MAP amendment
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@stellardata.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@stellardata.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short MAP shift due to PO timing

Hi Neha,

Quick note from procurement here — we have an internal PO approval window that slipped by two weeks (legal needs extra review on data residency language). That pushes our planned P0 evaluation start out of the original MAP by ~14 days. We still want to proceed with the canary evaluation but need a containment plan so the external launch gating doesn't drift further.

Can you propose a constrained rebaseline that preserves the October evaluation window (canary + ramp) inside a compressed decision lane? If we can agree to a short-term credit extension and a reduced scope canary (single workload), we can keep momentum. Attached is the draft PO and our procurement note.

Thanks —
Emily
Emily Zhao
Head of Platform, Stellar Data
attachments: procurement-po-draft.docx (docx), procurement-note.pdf (pdf)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@stellardata.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@stellardata.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short MAP shift due to PO timing

Emily — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the PO draft. We can work this into a short containment protocol that minimizes risk to the close date. High level proposal (quick):

- Compression window: move formal P0 gate by +10 business days but run an internal canary as originally scheduled (single-customer workload) on Oct 6.
- Scope reduction: canary focused on latency/throughput for the one critical pipeline (no full data migration).
- Credit buffer: grant a one-time evaluation credit to cover canary runs through Oct 15; this keeps usage friction low while procurement finalizes.
- Escalation: route legal questions to our compliance SME for targeted language edits (cc'd Soojin).

I attached a MAP-draft with the compressed lane (MAP-draft_v1.3.pdf) and a timeline-comparison.xlsx so we can visualize risk. If that sounds OK I will 1) update the mutual action plan, 2) open the amendment DocuSign (Marissa will review for approvals), and 3) create a short risk log and owner roster.

Quick ask to internal team: can Marissa or Jonas flag any account-level constraints (discounts / credits / SLA exceptions) we should track before committing?

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
attachments: MAP-draft_v1.3.pdf (pdf), timeline-comparison.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commitment stretch: containment protocol and MAP amendment

Neha / Marissa — digging into the risks. I sketched a short risk ledger we should include in the MAP amendment and the exec note: 

1) Risk R-01 (Procurement delay): Impact = P0 gate shift; Mitigation = compressed canary + one-time credit; Owner = Neha.
2) Risk R-02 (Legal language on data residency): Impact = possible further delay; Mitigation = Soojin to propose redline by 10/4; Owner = Soojin.
3) Risk R-03 (Performance variance on production-like traffic): Impact = longer ramp; Mitigation = narrow canary scope + run fixed traffic profile; Owner = Jonas (infra).
4) Risk R-04 (Commercial approval / discount signoff): Impact = budget hold; Mitigation = Marissa to approve temporary evaluation credit and DocuSign amendment; Owner = Marissa.

Recommendation: define a 7-day observation window after the internal canary (Oct 6 + 7 days) after which we formally re-evaluate the gate. If any of the top-two risks materialize we move to an escalated decision lane (exec review on 10/15).

I will draft the short risk table and owner commitments and drop into the MAP draft. Also confirming we can provide the evaluation credit for the compressed period — Marissa, can you confirm the credit quantum and sign-off path?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@stellardata.com>, Alex Chen <alex@stellardata.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Commitment stretch: containment protocol and MAP amendment

Emily / Alex — we spoke internally and can accept the compressed lane you requested. Summary and next steps: 

- Agreement: Redwood will proceed with the narrowed canary on Oct 6 (single workload) and provide a one-time evaluation credit that covers canary usage through Oct 15.
- MAP amendment: Neha will push MAP-draft_v1.3.pdf with the risk ledger embedded and open a DocuSign amendment for the updated milestone dates (link below).
- Legal path: Soojin will deliver a targeted redline addressing data residency language by EOD 10/04.
- Escalation triggers: if the internal canary shows >10% performance variance or legal redline cannot be resolved by 10/04, we escalate to Exec Review (scheduled tentatively for 10/15).

Action items:
- Neha: update MAP + send DocuSign (due 10/02)
- Soojin: redline legal language (due 10/04)
- Jonas: prepare canary traffic script and runbook (due 10/05)
- Marissa: approve evaluation credit (applied immediately) and own exec escalation if needed

DocuSign (amendment preview): https://www.docusign.com/embedded/abcd-1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4632

Emily — please confirm that the compressed lane is acceptable on your side and that procurement can sign the PO amendment once the DocuSign is complete. If yes, Neha will send the MAP amendment and we will proceed to the canary plan.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
attachments: MAP-draft_v1.3.pdf (pdf), timeline-comparison.xlsx (xlsx)
